messages:

Cc: Northvale IT <it@northvale.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Kube landing: inventory + disk encryption questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks for taking this on. We're doing a preflight for our first on-prem deployment of Redwood private (VPC-connected) at our Boston colocation. We attached an inventory export (nv-site-inventory.xlsx) with rack-level servers and public/private VLAN mappings. A few specific asks from infra/security: 

- Confirm whether Redwood needs a dedicated control-plane VLAN vs. shared management VLAN for k8s API servers.
- Storage: we're planning on NVMe-backed block devices for pods, and a separate NFS layer for long-term artifacts. Do you advise encrypted LUKS at the host or relying on customer-managed KMS/HSM integration?
- Node pools: we plan a dedicated GPU pool + mixed CPU types for inference workers. Any guidance on node labeling and eviction thresholds?

Can we schedule a 45-min technical checklist review next week? I've bcc'd procurement to keep them in the loop.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Operations
Northvale Financial

Attachment: nv-site-inventory.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet, ~120 rows)
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@northvale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kube landing: inventory + disk encryption questions

Elena —

Appreciate the inventory. Reviewed at a high level, looks healthy. Preliminary answers below and a few requests so we can finalize the preflight checklist: 

- Control-plane VLAN: recommend a dedicated management VLAN for API/control-plane traffic. Reasons: simpler microsegmentation for kube-apiserver ports, easier audit capture, and avoids noisy tenant east-west traffic impacting control-plane latency. We can support a consolidated setup if you have strict VLAN limits, but will call out the tradeoffs in the checklist.

- Storage encryption: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integration (KMIP or cloud KMS via VPN). For host disks we prefer full-disk encryption managed by your KMS/HSM (LUKS with remote key wrapping) so that snapshot/backup artifacts remain encrypted at rest. If you prefer host-level LUKS, ensure keys are rotated and accessible prior to node bootstrap.

- Node pools & labels: recommend three pools initially: gpu-inference (GPU, high-memory), compute-worker (CPU-optimized), and infra (small, tainted for agents/metrics/logging). Use labels: 
  - nodepool="gpu-inference"
  - nodeclass="highmem-gpu"
  - env="prod"

Eviction thresholds: default kube eviction is fine for starters; we suggest setting kube-reserved & system-reserved to protect KV cache. We'll produce a quick node-sizing CSV.

Action items for you before the call: share any host-level key management requirements and confirm whether NFS is provided by an existing SAN team or if you want us to proposed an appliance. Also please share the expected per-pod disk/IO profile for model caching.

I'll loop in Rishi (runtime) and Marissa (delivery) for sizing and rollout planning. Proposed call: Tue 17 Jul 2028 10:30am ET. Does that work?

- Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kube landing: inventory + disk encryption questions

Adding node sizing and operational notes from delivery:

- Node sizing (initial recommendation):
  * gpu-inference: 4 x A40-equivalent nodes (48 vCPU / 384GB / 80GB GPU mem) for the first rack; add autoscale + burst pool.
  * compute-worker: 8 x 32v / 128GB nodes for batch preprocessing and non-latency inference.
  * infra: 3 x 8v / 32GB nodes (tainted) for logging, monitoring, and control-plane support if you don't want dedicated masters.

- Storage classes:
  * fast-block (local NVMe): for model KV cache and ephemeral caching. Recommend ext4/XFS with discard disabled and best-effort file ownership enforcement.
  * durable-block (iSCSI/SAN): for persistent datasets, snapshots enabled.
  * archive-nfs: for long-term artifacts (daily snapshots).

- I/O policies: for GPU nodes, reserve 20% of IO bandwidth for system to avoid eviction storms during model downloads.

- Eviction & QoS: set system-reserved cpu/memory to 500m / 1Gi and kube-reserved to 500m / 1Gi on GPU nodes. Pod-level QoS enforced via requests/limits.

I'll attach a basic node-sizing CSV (node-sizing-proposal.csv) and a draft rollout timeline after the call.

Marissa
Senior Delivery Manager
Redwood Inference
